<objective>
Produce the one number this phase cannot borrow, and the fixture corpus without which nothing
downstream can be tested.

D-10 mandates that `MAP_MAX_BYTES` be MEASURED. RESEARCH § O-03 establishes that no existing constant
substitutes: SPIKE-06's operation set is `read, decode, hash, hash_js_loop, vlq_decode, tokenize,
parse` and contains no `JSON.parse` at all. D-08 puts that parse on the proxy thread, which makes the
number load-bearing rather than informational.

RESEARCH also found, by measurement, that **no pinned corpus bundle carries an inline map** — all
three announcing bundles announce external `.map` files. So the fixtures this probe needs do not
exist and must be built, and they are the same fixtures MAP-05 and D-15 need. One artifact, three
consumers, and it comes first.

Purpose: everything downstream — the D-02 tail window, the D-14 derived-path bound, MAP-06's
aggregate limit, the viewer's line cap — is derived from this result instead of extrapolated.
Output: a schema-validated probe artifact, a gate that reads it, a tracked fixture corpus, and four
new constants in `thresholds.ts` whose derivations are written down.
</objective>

  <action>
Widen the tracer to the full measurement, and build the fixture module three plans read.

**The ladder.** Extend `scripts/phase7/map-bytes.sh` to four points of DECODED map JSON — roughly
0.5, 1.5, 3 and 6.29 MB — matching SPIKE-06's ladder shape and topping out at the structural ceiling
rather than above it. ONE FRESH INSTANCE PER POINT, non-negotiable: RSS is a high-water mark that
never falls, the allocator does not return pages to the OS, and there is no `gc()`, so reusing an
instance makes every point after the first meaningless. Each point gets its own `run_id`.

**The operations.** Extend `tier1/mapbytes/src/index.ts` to the five operations RESEARCH § O-03
specifies, in this fixed order with the heaviest last: `announce_scan`, `b64_decode_atob`,
`b64_decode_buffer`, `json_parse`, `sources_materialise`. `sources_materialise` iterates
`map.sourcesContent` and hashes each entry with the native `createHash` — `JSON.parse` alone does not
tell you what holding 781 strings costs, and that is where peak RSS actually lands. Measure BOTH
base64 primitives: the delta is the argument for choosing, and Pitfall 4 says the wrong one corrupts
non-ASCII recovered source silently.

**The opportunistic retention observation.** While an instance is up, store N requests, wait, re-`get`
them and record the survival curve as an `observations` member of the artifact with its own `status`
field. RESEARCH Open Question 1 says do not block on it; record it as an observation and never as a
settled retention policy.

**The verdict.** Fill `verdict.answer` with the derived `MAP_MAX_BYTES` and `verdict.if_wrong` with
RESEARCH § O-03's two outcomes: below the ceiling means the phase recovers source from a minority of
inline maps and must say so in the UI; at the ceiling means the bound is non-binding and the D-02
window is the full base64 span. Record the O-04 finding in the same object: MAP-02's
`781 sources / 12.66 MB / 21 ms` figure was taken in standalone quickjs-ng 0.16.1 per
`.planning/research/STACK.md:546`, and under D-01 plus `PASSIVE_MAX_BYTES` that case cannot arise
because 12.66 MB base64-encodes to roughly 16.9 MB.

**The fixture corpus, and the tracked-home decision that PATTERNS demands be made explicitly.**
`corpus/` is gitignored in its entirety (`.gitignore:9`), so RESEARCH § O-03's instruction to commit
fixtures under `corpus/maps/` is NOT followed — bytes written there do not survive a clean checkout.
The corpus splits by size across the two tracked homes PATTERNS identifies:

  - **Large real maps** (megabyte scale, needed only by the probe) go to `scripts/phase7/fetch-maps.sh`
    with committed SHA-256 hashes, in the `fetch-corpus.sh` idiom. Bytes stay gitignored; the script
    and its hashes are the reproducible artifact.
  - **Small hostile and structural fixtures** (needed by CI on every commit, with no network) go to
    `packages/engine/src/sourcemap/map-fixture.ts` as string literals, in the `hostile.fixture.ts`
    idiom — one module, every consumer asserting the id array IN FULL.

`packages/engine/src/sourcemap/map-fixture.ts` exports three frozen arrays and three id arrays
derived from them, with a header stating the one-module rule and the escape-not-literal rule in
`hostile.fixture.ts`'s register:

  - `HOSTILE_MAP_CASES` — structural hostility: `sourcesContent` absent entirely; `sourcesContent`
    shorter than `sources`; a null entry in `sourcesContent`; a null entry in `sources`; a `sections`
    index map; a NESTED `sections` map (must be refused); an unsorted/overlapping `sections` map; a
    `sections` member whose `map` is null; a `)]}'` XSSI prefix; JSON nested past the measured
    246-paren / 710-bracket stack limits; a map declaring millions of tiny sources; a map with one
    giant `sourcesContent` entry; a non-ASCII round-trip case carrying a pound sign, an em dash and a
    CJK character.
  - `SOURCES_LABEL_CASES` — all 22 SPIKE-12 `path_resolution` strings verbatim, ids matching SPIKE-12's
    `variant` names so the provenance is greppable, PLUS a 23rd case: a 4 KB label, the one class
    SPIKE-12 does not cover. Size the 4 KB label just above `TABLE_CELL_MAX_GRAPHEMES` and just above
    the source-line cap plan 07-07 declares, so the truncation boundary is exercised from both sides.
  - `SIZE_BOUNDARY_CASES` — a decoded map at exactly `MAP_MAX_BYTES` and one at `MAP_MAX_BYTES + 1`,
    generated by repetition rather than written out, in `MULTI_MEGABYTE`'s idiom.

Every adversarial character is an escape sequence. A literal C0 control or RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE is
invisible in every diff and every review tool, and this corpus is entirely about characters that are
invisible.

`tests/corpus-maps.spec.ts` is the fixture gate: it asserts every case id is unique, that no case
`value` is the empty string except the one case whose id declares it, that the id arrays are exported
and non-empty, and that `scripts/phase7/fetch-maps.sh` declares exactly one committed SHA-256 per
fetched file with no placeholder.
  </action>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| jsDelivr CDN → probe fixtures | Three unreviewed minified sourcemaps enter the measurement path |
| fixture file on disk → QuickJS `JSON.parse` | Attacker-shaped JSON crosses into the runtime under measurement |
| Caido CLI binary → measurement record | A wrong or drifted build silently produces a wrong number |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-07-14 | Tampering | `scripts/phase7/map-bytes.sh` target binary | high | mitigate | Own pinned `MAP_PROBE_EXPECTED_VERSION = "0.58.0"` asserted before any recording; target is the in-repo sha512-verified `.caido-bin/0.58.0/caido-cli`; `~/.caido/caido-cli` (stale 0.55.3) refused by name; Phase 1's and Phase 6's constants untouched |
| T-07-18 | Tampering | `scripts/phase7/fetch-maps.sh` | high | mitigate | Every fetch pinned to an immutable versioned jsDelivr path AND gated on a committed SHA-256; a mismatch deletes the file and exits non-zero rather than measuring something nobody chose. Fixture bytes are read, hashed and parsed but never evaluated |
| T-07-03 | Denial of service | `JSON.parse` in `tier1/mapbytes` | medium | mitigate | Deep-nesting cases are bounded by the measured 246-paren / 710-bracket stack limits; SPIKE-06 measured the failure is a catchable `RangeError` every time and the host survived all 18 probes, so the probe catches and records rather than crashing the instance |
| T-07-19 | Information disclosure | probe instance guest token | low | accept | `instance.sh` mints a per-run guest bearer token under `umask 077`, `chmod 600`, and deletes it at teardown. Inherited unchanged; no new secret and no new env var |
| T-07-20 | Repudiation | `map-bytes.json` provenance | medium | mitigate | `run_id` UNIQUENESS asserted across points, not merely `fresh: true`; the gate fails and names the remedy rather than skipping when the artifact is absent |
| T-07-SC | Tampering | npm/pnpm installs | high | mitigate | This plan installs nothing. No `pnpm add`, no lockfile change, no new dependency. The D-16 codec relocation and its package-legitimacy disposition belong to plan 07-03 |
</threat_model>

## Planner assumptions carried forward, flagged rather than settled

- **A1 (RESEARCH):** `JSON.parse` of a bounded map is affordable somewhere below 6.29 MB on the proxy
  thread. This is the phase's premise and this plan is its mitigation. If the probe finds it
  affordable nowhere useful, D-08's always-on placement needs revisiting and that is a CONTEXT-level
  escalation, not a planner decision.
- **A2 (RESEARCH):** `lastIndexOf` over a multi-MB string is cheap enough for the derived tail window.
  Unmeasured anywhere; `announce_scan` is in this probe's operation list precisely to settle it. If it
  is expensive, the recorded mitigation is a 16-byte `lastIndexOf("sourceMappingURL")` prefilter.
- **A6 (RESEARCH):** mainstream bundlers put the announcement on the last line. Measured true for 3/3
  announcing corpus bundles, but n=3 and all three are external. An inline map placed mid-file would
  be missed and this plan does not close that.
